original_question: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. What formula governs T112(3n+1, 3n+1) for n >= 1?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 9 ("Both stones, two kinds of bones"): Find a formula governing T112(3n+1, 3n+1).
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper’s intended target almost exactly: it identifies the type-112 model (both stone orientations allowed, exactly two bone orientations allowed), the correct benzel family (3n+1, 3n+1), and the correct quantifier n >= 1. This is essentially Problem 9 in Section 7.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should say that T112(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel by translates of the five prototiles restricted to the right stone, the left stone, and exactly two of the three bone prototiles.
It should note that, by the paper’s threefold-rotational symmetry reduction, T112 depends only on the fact that two bone orientations are allowed, not on which specific bone orientation is forbidden.
It should explicitly frame the task as finding an explicit formula governing the sequence T112(3n+1,3n+1) for every integer n >= 1.
If the question is to be self-contained outside the paper, it should identify the benzel as the finite hexagonal-grid region defined in Section 1.
The nearby context records an empirical observation that, for T(n)=T112(3n+1,3n+1), no prime factor of T(n) appears to be >= 4n; this is contextual motivation, not part of the official problem.
No ambient ring/field, operator, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large' clause is involved here; this is a purely combinatorial tiling-enumeration problem.
refined_question: Let T112(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel by translates of the right stone, the left stone, and any fixed two of the three bone prototiles (vertical, rising, and falling), so that only the number of allowed bone orientations matters. For each integer n >= 1, find an explicit formula governing T112(3n+1, 3n+1).
justification: The draft is targeting Section 7 rather than a neighboring part of the paper. After defining Tijk(a,b) in Section 1 and identifying type 112 as the case of both stones plus two bone orientations, the paper turns in Section 7 to the type-112 central diagonals. There, after Table 8 and the accompanying remark about prime factors, Propp states exactly: 'Problem 9: Find a formula governing T112(3n+1, 3n+1).' This distinguishes the target from Problem 8, which concerns a conjectural second-quotient formula for T112(3n,3n), and from Problems 10–13, which concern other diagonals.
